bugs.title: Super Series prompt/routing gap - ROUND 4 (2026-09-13): bot Telegram 'Agent prompt' message still rendered the ordinary single-part 'SERIES MODE - this is Part 1' clause for Super Series anchor jobs
bugs.notes: OPERATOR RE-REPORT (2026-09-13): 'The issue seems to be fixed but the AI agent prompt in the bot is still showing series part 1.' ROUND 4 ROOT CAUSE (verified against live data and live code, not re-derived): rounds 1-3 had fixed (r1) the missing set:superseries* handlers, (r2) buildStageARequest stripping series.super_series on persist, (r3) verified the release 00_READ_THIS_FIRST.txt carries the SUPER_SERIES_DIRECTIVE. This session re-verified ALL of that against the operator's NEWEST flow before touching code: branding/super_series_settings.json enabled:true; anchor job manual-1789258181075 (created after ALL prior fixes) has stage-a-request.json with series.super_series:true; its LIVE release asset 00_READ_THIS_FIRST.txt (downloaded from release tag clipforge-manual-1789258181075) opens with '## SUPER SERIES MODE - YOU ARE PLANNING THE WHOLE SERIES IN ONE DOCUMENT' and contains NO ordinary single-part directive; the super-plan uploaded against it validated and routed correctly - jobs/manual-1789258181075/super-plan.json shows 4 parts with sequential spawn p1->p2->p3 actively rendering. THE ONE REMAINING GAP: sendAgentPrompt (bot/src/index.js), the function that renders the 'Agent prompt - Task <label>' Telegram message + the tap-to-copy copy_text button, built its series clause from series.enabled ALONE and never consulted series.super_series - so for a Super Series anchor the bot message still said 'SERIES MODE - this is Part 1 of series ...' with a single-part production.json ask, exactly matching the operator's screenshot/symptom. Every prior round's tests asserted the settings handlers, the persisted request, and the pipeline template - but NOTHING asserted the text of the bot's handoff message, which is the artifact the operator actually reads. Same class of gap as r1/r2: each layer correct in isolation, the seam between them (request file -> Telegram message text) unpinned. FIX (surgical, bot/src/index.js only): sendAgentPrompt now derives isSuperSeries = reqSeries.super_series === true and (a) renders a SUPER SERIES MODE clause ('plan the WHOLE series ... in ONE document ... NOT a single-part production.json ... one JSON document with version 2 and a parts array ...') in place of the ordinary Part-N clause; (b) changes the ask line to 'Produce exactly one WHOLE-SERIES super-plan document'; (c) gives the copy_text button a dedicated 3-tier super ladder (super-plan wording + series id in every tier) chosen by longest-fits-250, falling back to the ordinary ladder only if even the shortest super entry overflows - the ordinary ladder itself is UNCHANGED for ordinary jobs. ORDINARY-PATH PRESERVATION: the shared ordinary copy ladder (bug-15) is byte-identical for non-super jobs; verified by test. NOTE on ordinary-path copy_text: with any realistic release URL the ordinary ladder overflows 250 chars before the compact series clause fits, so ordinary jobs' copy_text carries the bare prompt (Part clause lives in the full message/pre block) - pre-existing behavior, unchanged, pinned by test. VERIFICATION (all against the real worker via handleUpdate->handleCallback->routeCallback->handleTaskCallback->sendAgentPrompt with stubbed fetch, asserting the EXACT Telegram message text + copy_text payload): NEW bot/test/super-series-agent-prompt.test.mjs - 4 tests: (1) super anchor prompt says SUPER SERIES MODE, pins series id, asks for the whole-series super-plan, contains NO 'this is Part 1'/'Series part 1' anywhere in message, <pre>, or copy_text, copy_text <=256 and carries super-plan wording; (2) ordinary series job KEEPS 'this is Part 1 of series' in the message and gets NO Super Series wording in copy_text; (3) series-less job renders neither clause; (4) super_series:1 (truthy non-true) does NOT switch the clause (gate is === true, matching the upload router and bundle.py dispatch). FULL SUITES: bot 252/252 pass (248 prior + 4 new); pipeline test_super_series.py 15/15 pass. END-TO-END LIVE STATE (re-verified this round, from origin/main + live GitHub release): settings enabled:true -> wizard commit boundary sets wizard.superSeries -> wizardToRequest emits series.super_series -> buildStageARequest persists it -> bundle.py dispatches --super-series -> prompt.py emits SUPER_SERIES_DIRECTIVE in the release prompt -> upload router (index.js:1341) routes super-plans to handleSuperPlanUploadMessage -> sequential queue spawns parts. The bot handoff message was the last link still showing the old wording; it is now wired. DEPLOY: .github/workflows/deploy-bots.yml runs tests + wrangler deploy of Bot A/B on push to the central repo's main, so THIS push triggers the redeploy - no manual operator step beyond using a task whose prompt is requested AFTER the deploy lands. Existing in-flight super parts (series-1789258211391-p1..p3) are per-part executors and are unaffected.
